title: UNIFORMAT II — elemental classification (ASTM E1557 lineage, CSI 1998 edition)
_status_note: 'verified-from-data' means the DETECT block and the observed code shapes below were EXTRACTED from
a real building in this fleet, not copied from memory. Source: internal/UNMERGED/Hospital_IFC4_*.ifc,
re-extracted 2026-07-30, 4546 coded elements / 15 distinct codes. See evidence.observed_codes.
⚠ WHAT IS *NOT* VERIFIED: the authoritative document is ASTM E1557, which this repo does NOT hold.
Only levels 3 (5 chars) and 4 (8 chars) were OBSERVED. Levels 1 (1 char) and 2 (3 chars) are
permitted by the pattern because the observed codes are strict prefix-extensions of them, but no
level-1 or level-2 code appears in our data. Do not present the level table as sourced from ASTM.

segments.name: major_group
segments.description: Major group letter. OBSERVED in our data: A, B, C, D.
segments._values_note: A/B/C/D are corroborated by the reference NAMES our own extract carries (e.g. A1010130 'Pile Caps' = Substructure, D2090800 'Piping & Fittings' = Services). E/F/G are NOT observed in our data — treat as unverified until the ASTM source is held.

segments.name: group_element
segments.description: Group element, e.g. B|20 = Exterior Enclosure, D|20 = Plumbing, D|40 = Fire Protection.

segments.name: individual_element
segments.description: Individual element. First OBSERVED level: D4090 'Other Fire Protection Systems' (5 chars).

segments.name: sub_element
segments.description: Sub-element / assembly. The 8-char form, 14 of our 15 observed codes.

element.note: the only facet this scheme codes; Uniformat is elemental, not spatial

space.note: Uniformat has no space/room code — use OmniClass Table 13 or Uniclass SL

level.note: Uniformat has no storey code — see locales.json level_naming

system.note: the D major group is service-system shaped (D20 Plumbing, D40 Fire Protection, D50 Electrical) but it codes the ELEMENT, not a system instance

evidence._length_note: D4090 is 5 chars while every other observed code is 8. A fixed-width validator would have rejected a code the authoring tool really wrote. This is the concrete reason 'permitted_lengths' is a list.
